falsifiers: A missing observation required by a wake condition must classify as UNKNOWN/ABSTAIN_NOT_OBSERVED, not silently as NO_MATCH and never as MATCH.

Wake matching must be a pure function over explicit caller-supplied condition and observation values; reading wall clock, sensors, UnifiedDB, environment state or network state inside the component violates the workpackage boundary.
A matched wake condition may emit only an explicit match/resume-candidate receipt. It must not mutate Goal lifecycle state, schedule a process, invoke Persistent Pulse, or resume execution itself.
Time-based conditions, if supported, must compare against an explicit observed-time value supplied in the observation packet rather than calling a clock API internally.
Every evaluation must reject stale or mismatched hold/state identity, generation and state-digest fences; a valid evaluation cannot silently bind to a newer checkpoint.

Unknown condition types, malformed observations, ambiguous duplicate observation identities and type-mismatched comparison operands must fail closed or classify UNKNOWN, never be coerced into a positive match.
An unrelated observation or state change must not wake a hold merely because it is newer; the explicit condition identity and typed predicate must match.
Condition matching must preserve type semantics: boolean/integer/string/time/event identifiers cannot be silently normalized across types to create a match.

Wake/hold receipts must deterministically bind hold identity, prior state generation/digest, condition identity, observation identity/provenance, evaluation result and non-authoritative classification.
A wake MATCH must not grant goal adoption, effect authorization, completion verification, provider/tool authority or world-truth status.
